subject: Horizon Solutions starter kit — technical onboarding & partner enablement
messages:
From: Elliot Barnes <elliot@horizoncloud.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Lara Gonzalez <lara.gonzalez@horizoncloud.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Horizon Solutions starter kit & proposed enablement flow

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. As discussed, attached is a lightweight starter kit for Horizon Cloud to run a two-week technical pilot with Redwood Inference. The ZIP contains: an architecture diagram, a proposed mutual action plan (MAP), and a short ops checklist.

High-level ask:
- 2-week pilot focused on: inference latency profiling (RPS 50–200), model routing proof-of-concept, and cost reporting hooks.
- Partner enablement sessions: 90m technical kickoff, two 60m deep-dive workshops (runtime/ops + integrations), and a final 45m wrap review.

What we need from Redwood to move forward:
1) Confirmation of a technical owner for kickoff (to lead the workshop).
2) A short dev checklist for pre-kickoff (test keys, request samples, sandbox access).
3) A proposed calendar window (we are targeting Jun 21 — Jul 2).

I attached the starter materials: starterkit-architecture-diagram.pdf and horizon-mutual-action-plan.xlsx.

If this looks good, can we lock a 90m slot for the kickoff the week of Jun 21?

Thanks,
Elliot Barnes
Solutions Lead — Horizon Cloud Solutions
elliot@horizoncloud.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

[attachment: starterkit-architecture-diagram.pdf] [attachment: horizon-mutual-action-plan.xlsx]

Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Horizon Solutions starter kit & proposed enablement flow

Elliot —

Really helpful, thanks for sending the MAP and architecture diagram. I reviewed the attachments and added a one-page enablement outline (attached) that maps Redwood owners to the workshop agenda and required artifacts.

Quick answers up front:
- Technical owner for kickoff: Jonas Weber (cc’d) will own the runtime/ops kickoff and the latency profiling session.
- Pre-kickoff checklist: see the attached "redwood-enablement-outline.pdf" — it includes test API key scope, sample corpus guidance, and a sandbox provisoning checklist.
- Calendar: Jun 22 or Jun 24 both look promising for a 90m kickoff from our side. Can you confirm which you prefer?

Open items we need from Horizon before we kick:
- A representative request sample (500–2k tokens typical) and target SLAs for p50/p95 latency.
- Any network egress constraints for the sandbox (our private sandbox can be restricted by CIDR).

Next steps: once you confirm date + sample, Jonas will publish a short runbook and Priyom will provision a temporary test instance and share creds through our secure vault.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Partner Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

Team — forwarding Horizon's starter kit and my reply. Quick internal checklist before we lock the Jun 22/24 kickoff: 

Priority tasks:
- Jonas: lead the 90m kickoff (runtime deep-dive). Prepare a 15m latency baseline demo and a short warm-up lab for attendees. Bring one slide that explains our fallback/model-variant routing behavior.
- Priyom: stand up the sandbox instance (gpu-dev-pp-sandbox) with the sample model and deploy a sample tracing hook for token-level cost telemetry. Share temporary creds via Vault and add elliot@horizoncloud.ai as a view-only user on the sandbox.
- Mina (me): own MAP alignment and the partner-facing agenda; I'll own logistics and the slide deck. Also confirm whether Horizon needs any additional compliance paperwork before the pilot (SOC2 excerpt, IP clause).

Risks/notes:
- We need a Horizon sample payload by EOD Thu (10 Jun) to finalize the lab. Without representative inputs we risk not hitting realistic p95.
- If we bump the kickoff past Jun 24, we'll need to compress the workshop cadence. Flagging for sales.

I've attached the external MAP for quick reference.

Thanks — please reply with confirmations and I'll update the MAP and calendar invite.

Mina
